Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 25-year-old woman with 2-month history of escalating anxiety temporally related to starting a new, stressful job. Somatic features include insomnia (3–4 h/night) and morning palpitations lasting up to 10 min. Functional impact: dread of work, reduced enjoyment of exercise and social activities, low daytime energy.  
• No prior psychiatric history; no suicidal thoughts; supportive family.  
• Likely diagnoses: adjustment disorder with anxiety vs evolving generalized anxiety disorder; possible mixed anxiety-depressive features. Physical contributors (thyrotoxicosis, anemia, arrhythmia) considered low probability but being screened via basic bloods.  
• Management agreed: self-referral to NHS talking therapies (CBT), provision of online anxiety/sleep resources, lifestyle advice, routine blood tests, GP follow-up after results. Patient advised to seek earlier review if symptoms worsen or interfere with functioning. No pharmacotherapy initiated at this stage.

Management Plan
- Self-refer to NHS talking therapy service (link to be sent).  
- Begin recommended online CBT/anxiety and sleep hygiene resources immediately.  
- Arrange “basic blood tests” (likely FBC, iron profile, TFTs, electrolytes, glucose) via support line; GP review 1 week post-testing.  
- Safety-netting: Contact GP urgently if anxiety escalates, work attendance becomes impossible, or any self-harm thoughts arise.  
- No medication started today; may reconsider after therapy/blood results.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Adjustment disorder with anxiety (High) – Clear temporal link to new job; pervasive worry, insomnia, palpitations.  
2. Emerging generalized anxiety disorder / mixed anxiety-depressive disorder (Moderate) – Symptoms approaching GAD criteria; low mood and anhedonia present.  
3. Hyperthyroidism (Low–Medium) – Palpitations and insomnia could mimic anxiety; screening planned.
